title: km/h to m/s? Unit Conversion Explained Simply | PUC Physics Class 11
description:
A tailor uses inches, a road sign uses km/h and the physics book wants m/s. Aarav's bicycle meter reads 18 km/h, and his homework wants it in metres per second. Is it still 18? In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Physics (NCERT Chapter 1, Units and Measurement) we learn to convert any unit in one line, and never get it backwards.

Ride with Aarav on a live motion notebook: road markers in metres, a slow-mo replay of the first second and an x-t graph whose slope is the speed, in two units. We build the conversion factor (a fraction equal to 1), derive the famous 5/18 step by step, see why km/h to m/s divides by 3.6, and learn why squared and cubed units need a squared or cubed factor. Two pause-and-think questions, a worked example (water: 1 g/cm³ = 1000 kg/m³), the 18/5 exam trap, an original JEE Main pattern question on g in km/h², a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, JEE Main and NEET students.

In this video:
0:00 Same world, different units
0:26 What converting a unit means: the factor that equals 1
0:55 Aarav's ride: 18 km/h is 5 m/s, live
1:32 Derivation: 18 km/h to m/s in 5 steps
2:08 Why 5/18, link by link
2:38 Side by side + pause and think
3:07 Units with powers: 1 m² = 10,000 cm²
3:49 Worked example: density of water in kg/m³
4:28 Exam trap: 18/5 or 5/18?
4:53 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
5:26 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Dimensions of Physical Quantities. Can you add 5 metres to 5 seconds?
